title: Mark Zuckerberg has an Instagzam
excerpt: Plus, what’s in Mark Zuckerberg’s manifesto on the future of AI, the future of AI music, and more on this episode of The Vergecast.

On The Vergecast: Instagram’s new logo, Zuck’s AI manifesto, and lots of other bad ideas.

On The Vergecast: Instagram’s new logo, Zuck’s AI manifesto, and lots of other bad ideas.

by David Pierce

Aug 14, 2026, 4:54 PM UTC

David Pierce

is editor-at-large and Vergecast co-host with over a decade of experience covering consumer tech. Previously, at Protocol, The Wall Street Journal, and Wired.

Instagram’s wordmark is iconic. Well, was iconic. Apparently Instagram thought it looked old, so the company rolled out a new one this week. It doesn’t look like the old Instagram wordmark. It doesn’t even look like it spells Instagram anymore. And we cannot figure out why Instagram decided to do this.

On this episode of The Vergecast, David and Nilay start by discussing the new logo, the executive urge to redesign everything all the time, and whether new is always better. After that, they get into the other big Meta release of the week: Mark Zuckerberg’s many-thousand-word missive on the future of AI. There are a lot of ideas and proposals in the post, all centered on one really big, very Zuckerberg-y thesis: that if you give all the technology to everyone, everything will be fine. Quite a take from the guy who sees what happens on Facebook every day. (By the way, here’s the Meta Design Blog post we reference, and the incredible Pepsi branding doc.)

After that, it’s time for some more AI news, including a new way of “watermarking” AI-generated text, Apple’s stamp of reality, Spotify’s crackdown on AI artists (but not AI music), and some chaos in the guitar industry. Then it’s off to the lightning round, with news about Brendan Carr, ChatGPT, Flock, cheap phones, and more.

In case you missed it this week: We also talked about our vibe-coding projects, the first chatbot ever, the new Google Pixels, and the state of robot lawnmowers. And we want to hear all your thoughts about all of it! Call the Vergecast Hotline at 866-VERGE11, send us an email at vergecast@theverge.com, and tell us everything that’s on your mind. And make sure you subscribe so you don’t miss an episode!

On The Vergecast：Instagram 的新标志、扎克伯格的人工智能宣言，以及许多其他糟糕的想法。

作者：大卫·皮尔斯

世界标准时间 2026 年 8 月 14 日下午 4:54

大卫·皮尔斯

是特约编辑和 Vergecast 联合主持人，在消费技术领域拥有十多年的经验。 此前，曾供职于《Protocol》、《华尔街日报》和《连线》。

Instagram 的文字标记具有标志性。 嗯，是标志性的。 显然 Instagram 认为它看起来很旧，因此该公司本周推出了一款新产品。 它看起来不像旧的 Instagram 文字标记。 它甚至看起来不再是 Instagram 的拼写了。 我们不明白 Instagram 为何决定这么做。

在 The Vergecast 的这一集中，David 和 Nilay 首先讨论了新徽标、高管不断重新设计一切的冲动，以及新的是否总是更好。 之后，他们进入了本周的另一个重要元发布：马克·扎克伯格关于人工智能未来的数千字信件。 这篇文章中有很多想法和建议，都集中在一个非常大的、非常扎克伯格式的论点上：如果你把所有的技术给每个人，一切都会好起来的。 对于一个每天都在 Facebook 上看到动态的人来说，这真是太棒了。 （顺便说一句，这是我们参考的元设计博客文章，以及令人难以置信的百事可乐品牌文档。）

之后，是时候了解更多人工智能新闻了，包括为人工智能生成的文本添加“水印”的新方式、苹果的现实印记、Spotify 对人工智能艺术家（但不是人工智能音乐）的打压，以及吉他行业的一些混乱。 然后是闪电轮，包括有关 Brendan Carr、ChatGPT、Flock、廉价手机等的新闻。

如果您本周错过了：我们还讨论了振动编码项目、有史以来第一个聊天机器人、新的 Google Pixels 以及机器人割草机的现状。 我们想听听您对这一切的所有想法！ 请拨打 Vergecast 热线 866-VERGE11，发送电子邮件至 vergecast@theverge.com，并告诉我们您的所有想法。 并确保您订阅，这样您就不会错过任何一集！
